A1.justification: Despite the changed title and framing, both PDFs describe the same feature-kernel decomposition, minimum projection operator, and CKA-based diagnostic, with many matching experiments. The complete main texts and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original neural-network experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10/100, transfer-learning experiments, and synthetic approximation-validation results, including in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original image-classification and regression results and adds encoded-MNIST, modular-division grokking, and richness-metric comparison experiments.

M1.justification: The MP/CKA diagnostic remains the same under the rename from kappa_CKA to DLR, and the SVD formulations are equivalent. However, v2 Equation (5) squares the projector overlap for cumulative target quality, unlike v1 Equations (6)–(7). This changes the specified metric; whether it reflects changed calculations or an unexplained formula error is unresolved.

E1.justification: v2 adds MNIST with conflicting training/test label encodings, modular-division grokking, and a sine-basis regression example in Appendix C.2. It removes the MNIST/ImageNet-to-CIFAR-10 transfer-learning experiments and Gaussian feature-matrix validation. Standard MNIST/CIFAR coverage, the Heaviside example, and MNIST scalar regression remain.

E2.justification: v2 introduces evaluated richness comparators: initial-to-learned last-layer kernel alignment, squared parameter norm, NC1, and within-class covariance trace (Figure 2; Tables 3–4). These were not empirically compared against the diagnostic in v1. The explicit frozen-feature arm of v1's output-scaling comparison and the greedy-layerwise comparison in Figure 21 disappear, although frozen-feature comparisons remain elsewhere.

E3.justification: The MNIST scaling experiment changes from 10,000 samples with alpha values 1 and 100 in v1 Figure 6 to 1,000 samples with alpha values 0.2, 2, and 20 in v2 Figure 2(b). v2 also introduces transformer grokking protocols and reports 400-epoch CIFAR-100 experiments against v1's 600-epoch default. These are reported setting changes, without establishing reruns. v2 Figure 2(a)'s sample count remains inconsistent: its caption says 1,000, while Table 5 says 60,000.

E4.justification: v2 adds the weight-decay-dominated control testing misleading richness signals, the encoded-label shortcut analysis, and the feature-quality/intensity analysis in Figure 7. It removes width sweeps, stride comparisons, intermediate-layer analyses, and Nyström/QR validation from v1. Learning-rate, weight-decay, and ResNet cross-entropy analyses survive in v2 Appendix E.

E5.justification: v2 Appendix F.1 specifies that plot error bars represent one standard deviation over at least three runs, and Tables 2–4 report standard deviations for the principal new comparisons. v1 does not specify corresponding repeat counts or error-bar meanings. This establishes substantially expanded uncertainty reporting, without demonstrating an increase in runs for retained experiments.

E6.justification: New results include encoded-MNIST test accuracies of 10.0% versus 74.4% in v2 Figure 1 and grokking checkpoint accuracies of 5.2% and 99.8% in Figure 4. Retained entries also change: the ResNet18 epoch-200 diagnostic is 0.0031 in v1 Figure 5(a) and 0.026 in v2 Figure 16(a). Transfer-learning and approximation-validation results disappear. Revised settings prevent treating all numerical differences as same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: The MP-operator connection to neural collapse already exists in v1. v2 revises the NC1 formulation to use a pseudoinverse and supplies reorganized supporting reasoning. It also adds formal learnability and generalization-error expressions in Appendix C.2, changes the target-quality definition, and removes v1 Appendix E's second lemma and Appendix H's approximation-error derivations.

C1.justification: v1 foregrounds the MF/EF regime taxonomy, early feature collapse, hyperparameter relationships, and transfer-learning applications. v2 centers the contribution on measuring dynamical richness independently of representation quality, distinguishing lazy-to-rich transitions including grokking, and outperforming alternative richness proxies in diagnostic examples. The underlying visualization and neural-collapse connection remain central.

C2.justification: v2 develops specific interpretations involving greedy low-rank dynamics, excess features as an earlier-layer bottleneck, and limitations of competing richness proxies. It newly interprets simultaneous quality/intensity evolution as contrasting with silent alignment. Applicability is explicitly restricted to orthogonal, isotropic targets, while v1's detailed finite-sample approximation limitations and much of its finite-width discussion disappear.

D1.justification: v2 Appendix F adds experiment-specific sample counts, batch sizes, optimizer settings, schedules, implementation sources, and hardware, runtime, and memory information. It also documents regularization of the NC1 pseudoinverse. Conversely, v1's detailed architecture diagrams and QR-based orthogonalization instructions are removed. Their omission does not establish that the underlying implementations changed.

R1.justification: Research positioning shifts from a broad feature-learning, infinite-width, and transfer-learning survey toward low-rank dynamics and independent richness measurement. v2 adds substantial discussion of grokking and linear-network dynamics, citing works such as Kumar, Kunin, Lyu, Dominé, and Nam's 2025 position paper, while removing much of the earlier transfer-learning and finite-width literature.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, contribution list, and discussion are extensively rewritten around the new central question. Definitions, background, and examples are redistributed between the main text and appendices, and a dedicated comparison section is introduced. Terminology changes include MF/EF framing toward rich/lazy dynamics, kappa_CKA to DLR, and utility to utilization.

P2.justification: v2 adds encoded-MNIST illustrations, metric-comparison tables, grokking and feature-intensity plots, and summary, uncertainty, and settings tables. Existing displays are split, relocated, or redrawn: v1 Figure 4(b) becomes v2 Figure 5, and the Heaviside example moves to Figure 11. Architecture schematics and numerous validation plots are removed, substantially changing the visual organization.

improvement.justification: The sharper focus, direct metric stress tests, grokking evidence, and uncertainty reporting strengthen presentation and empirical support. However, v2 removes v1 Appendix H's validation of finite-sample failures and QR correction, leaves the changed quality formula unexplained, and gives conflicting sample counts for Figure 2(a). These losses and inconsistencies affect confidence in the central measurements, so the net quality direction remains uncertain despite the clear gains.
